mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates one signed difference to another, translate it directly as (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names and allowing the result to be negative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence describes "the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have" (or any similar phrasing).
mathgap.example: Treating the phrase as an absolute difference |A - B| = |C - D| instead of the signed form (A - B) = (C - D).

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person, set that person's current count to the stated number at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For sentences like "Tasha has 16 oranges" or any explicit count declaration.
mathgap.example: Assuming the count is final and ignoring later transfers that modify it.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All item counts must be non‑negative integers; after solving, discard any solution that yields a negative count for any person.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After obtaining a solution, verify each variable is ≥ 0.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution where a person ends up with -3 oranges.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For a transfer that is conditioned on a prior state, first evaluate the condition using the current counts, then apply the transfer only if the condition holds.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says something like "If X has at least N oranges, X gives N to Y".
mathgap.example: Applying the transfer regardless of whether X actually has enough oranges.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more oranges than Y" as X - Y = N (i.e., X = Y + N) and "X has N fewer oranges than Y" as X - Y = -N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence uses "more" or "fewer" to compare two quantities.
mathgap.example: Translating "X has 5 fewer oranges than Y" as X - Y = 5 instead of -5.

mathgap.title: Split‑all handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X splits all the items she owns equally among Y and Z", give each of Y and Z half of X's current count and set X's count to zero (unless the wording indicates otherwise).
mathgap.example: Giving each recipient half of X's items but forgetting to set X's count to zero.

mathgap.title: Targeted constraint extraction for queried variable
mathgap.principle: When the goal is to find a specific person's count, first collect all equations that directly involve that person (or are linked through a short chain) and focus solving effort on that subset.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, after parsing the problem, identify constraints involving the target variable.
mathgap.example: Solving the entire system of equations even though only a few involve the person of interest.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling with updated counts
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, updating their current counts for any subsequent statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any "X gives N to Y" statement.
mathgap.example: Using the giver's original count in later equations after they have already given away oranges.

mathgap.title: Substitution of known signed differences into signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: If a signed difference on one side of an equality is already known from a direct statement or previous deduction, substitute that known value into the equality to simplify and solve for unknowns.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering an equation of the form (A - B) = (C - D) where either side contains a previously determined difference.
mathgap.example: Leaving (Selena - Mittie) = (Marylee - Charley) unsimplified despite knowing (Mittie - Selena) = 3.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation of statements
mathgap.principle: Process the list of statements in the order given, using the current counts at each step; earlier equations may affect later ones, especially transfers.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Throughout solving, always respect the narrative order of the statements.
mathgap.example: Solving later equations with outdated counts because earlier transfers were ignored.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrasing "has more than" suggests a positive quantity, leading the model to take the absolute value instead of preserving sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate such statements directly as signed differences (A - B) = (C - D) without taking absolute values.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may treat all transfers as simultaneous, forgetting that later statements refer to updated counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process statements in the given order, updating counts after each transfer before using them in subsequent equations.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Direct count statements are taken as final values, overlooking later transfers that modify those counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct counts as the current count at that point; apply any later transfers to adjust them.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increase by N times' as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase can be read as adding N, but mathematically it means multiplying the original amount.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "increase by N times" as multiplying the original amount by (1 + N) or by N, depending on context.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting split‑all statements as leaving the original person with zero even when they are a recipient
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may think the original person always gives away all items, ignoring cases where they also receive a share.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply split‑all by dividing the original count among recipients and setting the original's count to zero only if the statement says they give away all items.
